source.author: verg
source.text: Respicimus: dira illuvies immissaque barba, consertum tegumen spinis; at cetera Graius, et quondam patriis ad Troiam missus in armis.
source.text_original: Respicimus: dira illuvies immissaque barba, / consertum tegumen spinis; at cetera Graius, / [et quondam patriis ad Troiam missus in armis.]
source.text_english: We look back: a hideous filth, and a beard let down, a covering woven with thorns; but in all else a Greek, and one once sent to Troy in his native armor.

reuse.author: val
reuse.text: et quem fama genus non est decepta Lyaei Phlias immissus patrios de vertice crines.
reuse.text_original: et quem fama genus non est decepta Lyaei / Phlias immissus patrios de vertice crines.
reuse.text_english: and Phlias, whom unerring rumor does not wrongly reckon among the family of Lyaeus, was sent down with his ancestral hair from the summit of his head.
